questions.question:
A battery with EMF \(E\) and internal resistance \(r\) is connected across a resistance \(R\). The power consumption in \(R\) will be maximum when:
1. \(R = 2r\)
2. \(R=\dfrac{r}{2}\)
3. \(R=\sqrt{2} r\)
4. \(R=r\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(P = I^2 R\) Step:Find the condition when power consumption in\(R\)will be maximum. Power delivered to the external resistance \(R\) is given by; \(P = I^2 R= \left(\dfrac{E}{R+r}\right)^2R~~~~~~~~\left[I = \dfrac{E}{R+r}\right]\) To maximize \(P\), differentiate with respect to \(R\)and set to zero i.e., \(\dfrac{dP}{dR} =0\). \(\Rightarrow \dfrac{dP}{dR}= \dfrac{d\left(\dfrac{E^2R}{(R+r)^2}\right)}{dR}=0\) After solving above expression, we get; \(R =r\) Therefore, for maximum power drawn across load,\({R}_{\text {Load }}={R}_{\text {intermal}}\)i.e.,\(R =r\). Hence, option (4) is the correct answer.

Two electric bulbs, rated at \({(25~\text W, 220~\text V)}\) and \((100~\text W, 220~\text V),\) are connected in series across a \(220~\text V\) voltage source. If the \(25~\text W\) and \(100~\text W\) bulbs draw powers \({P_1}\) and \({P_2}\) respectively, then:
1. \(P_1=16~\text W,~P_2=4~\text W \)
2. \(P_1=16~\text W,~P_2=9~\text W\)
3. \(P_1=9~\text W,~P_2=16~\text W\)
4. \(P_1=4~\text W,~P_2=16~\text W\)

Hint:\(P=\dfrac{V^2}{R} \) Step 1: Find the resistances of bulbs. For\(25\text{ W}\)bulb: \(R_1=\dfrac{220\times220}{5\times5}\) \(\Rightarrow R_1=44\times44~\Omega\) \(\Rightarrow R_1=4\times22\times22\) For\(100\text{ W}\)bulb: \(R_2=\dfrac{220\times220}{10\times10}\) \(\Rightarrow R_2=22\times22~\Omega\) Step 2: Find the total current when these two bulbs are connected in series. \(I=\dfrac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}}\) \(\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}}\) \(\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{220}{4\times22\times22+22\times22}\) \(\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{220}{5\times22\times22}\) \(\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{1}{11}\text{ A}\) Step 2: Find the power drawn by bulbs. For\(25\text{ W}\)bulb: \(P_1=I^2R_1\) \(\Rightarrow P_1=\dfrac{1}{11\times11}\times44\times44\) \(\Rightarrow P_1=16\text{ W}\) For\(100\text{ W}\)bulb: \(P_2=I^2R_2\) \(\Rightarrow P_2=\dfrac{1}{11\times11}\times22\times22\) \(\Rightarrow P_2=4\text{ W}\) Hence, option (1) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The figure shows three circuits \(\mathrm{I, II}\) and \(\mathrm{III}\) which are connected to a \(3~\text{V}\) battery. If the powers are dissipated by the configurations \(\mathrm{I, II}\) and \(\mathrm{III}\) are \({P}_1,{P}_2\) and \({P}_3\) respectively, then:

1. \({P}_3>{P}_2>{P}_1 \)
2. \({P}_2>{P}_1>{P}_3 \)
3. \({P}_1>{P}_3>{P}_2\)
4. \({P}_1>{P}_2>{P}_3\)
questions.explanation:
Hint:\(P=\dfrac{V^2}{R}\) Step:Find the correct order of power dissipated. In this question, we can compare the equivalent resistance of the three circuits because all are connected to the same \(3~\text{V}\) battery. \(P=\dfrac{V^2}{R}\) In circuit\(I\); The network is symmetric, so the two middle points are at the same potential. The effective resistance is\(R_{eq}= \dfrac{2\times 2}{2+2}= 1~\Omega\) \(\Rightarrow P_1 = \dfrac{3^2}{1} = 9~\text{W}\) In circuit \(II\); The effective resistance is given by; \(R_{eq} = 2||1||2 = \dfrac{1\times 1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}~\Omega\) \(\Rightarrow P_2 = \dfrac{3^2}{0.5} = 18~\text{W}\) In circuit \(III\); The effective resistance is given by; \(R_{eq} = 1+\dfrac{2\times 2}{2+2}=2~\Omega\) \(\Rightarrow P_3 = \dfrac{3^2}{2} = 4.5~\text{W}\) Therefore, the correct order of the power dissipated in the circuit is \({P}_2>{P}_1>{P}_3 \). Hence, option (2) is the correct answer.
